The bull market turned four this week 🎂

We also cover small caps vs higher yields, the dollar back above 100 on the DXY, and next week's midterm episode with PIMCO's Libby Cantrell.

Five bangers from Nathan Lambert:

1. China's compute gap:

"You talk to people [in China], and you're like, 'Oh, I heard an average OpenAI researcher has five thousand H100 equivalents that they can access at any time,' and like their jaw just falls to the floor. They're just like, 'I can't comprehend.'"

2. China's talent pool:

"The Chinese labs are very technically excellent... To say that China is anything but equal on talent, you're gonna have a hard time because they just have so many people being trained at such a high level."

3. OpenAI's superpower:

"[The frontier labs] have just taken the most ambitious bets the earliest in order to get there, and that's why OpenAI has done things like kickstart the reasoning model revolution."

"And I think that kind of breakthrough and that beautiful plot with the inference scaling laws is peak OpenAI. They're really good at getting this plot that just changes how everyone thinks about everything."

4. Underestimating the competition:

"The Chinese are so good at building models as well. I think there's a bit of cope where people are like, 'Only we are good at building models.' There are so many companies. There's, like, 20 to 30 companies that are building good models."

1. Sell the platform:

License the agent to a company to run in its own operations. No existing contract sets the price, so there's more upside, but new budgets take time to approve and results are harder to credit to the agent.

2. Sell the service:

Take over work a company already outsources, the way Red Ventures sold policies for insurers and got paid per policy closed. The budget already exists, so deals close faster, but the highest-value work usually runs in-house, which caps the upside.

3. Go full-stack:

Become the business, like buying debt portfolios and collecting on them yourself. You keep all the value the AI creates, but you also take on the licensing and compliance.
